goal.text: Build and keep up to date a savings plan (sinking fund) that, using a cash flow forecast, shows whether the person can cover each wedding payment on its due date from their own net income, existing savings and the expected family contribution.

origin.quote: saving to pay for the wedding

in.text: Saving enough from current monthly net income and the 10k already saved to meet the wedding payments
Timing of the three payments: fixed 6k due in 21 days, then 50% of the remaining cost 30 days before the wedding, then the other 50% 14 days before
The 20k contribution from the person's and partner's families, expected about 2 weeks before the wedding
An uncertain total cost that depends on guest count (about 200 invited; final count known the day before the 30-day payment)
Re-running the plan as guest numbers, dates and amounts change

out.text: Deciding whether to hold the wedding money in cash, savings or elsewhere
Building a full household budget or reorganising spending categories
How the wedding fits into wider finances (debt, investing, long-term goals, life after the wedding)
Tax advice or any recommendation on products

glossary.definition: Money set aside over a period of time for a known future expense. In personal budgeting it is a category you pay into regularly for a planned cost.
glossary.person_says: saving to pay for the wedding

glossary.definition: A plan that shows how much money is expected to come in and go out over a future period. For each period: closing balance = opening balance + expected money in - expected money out.
A specific amount to be saved by a set date for a particular purpose. The regular saving needed is the amount still to be saved divided by the number of periods until the date, ignoring interest.
Income after taxes and deductions. For an individual, take-home pay: the amount that actually reaches the bank account.
glossary.person_says: net pay (10k per month); first said 'gross' and then corrected it

glossary.definition: Total income before taxes, deductions or other withholdings. Net income is gross income minus taxes and deductions.
glossary.person_says: initially used 'gross income' for the 10k, then corrected it to net

glossary.definition: A way of tracking all the money coming in and how it is spent: list your income, sort your spending into categories, and compare the two.
glossary.person_says: 'current budget'; described as about 5k a month that they 'consume', which seems to mean monthly spending

particulars.what: The wedding cost is not fixed: it depends on guest count (about 200 invited now; final count known the day before the 30-day payment).
particulars.handling: Plan with an estimated total (ideally a low/high range) until the final count is confirmed, then recalculate the two instalments on the confirmed figure.

particulars.what: Payment schedule is a fixed 6k in 21 days, then two equal instalments of 50% each of the remaining cost, at 30 days and 14 days before the wedding.
particulars.handling: Treat 'remaining cost' as total cost minus the 6k, and each instalment as half of that. Confirm with the contract that the 6k counts toward the total.

particulars.what: A 20k contribution from the person's and partner's families is expected about 2 weeks before the wedding ('I think'; may change).
particulars.handling: Enter it as an inflow dated 14 days before the wedding, flagged as uncertain. Do not rely on it to fund the 6k or the 30-day payment, and update the date or amount when confirmed.

particulars.what: The person first called their 10k monthly income 'gross' and then corrected it to net.
particulars.handling: Use 10k per month net income (take-home pay). Check against payslips or bank deposits.

particulars.what: The person says they 'consume' about 5k a month.
particulars.handling: Read this as monthly spending (outflows) of about 5k, excluding wedding payments. Confirm that it covers all regular costs and whether it varies.

particulars.what: The person has 10k already saved for the wedding.
particulars.handling: Use it as the opening balance of the wedding fund in the forecast.

particulars.what: The person asked whether to upload bank statements or connect to the bank, or whether variation in spending matters.
particulars.handling: Not needed to start: use the 5k average for now. Statements can later be used to check the average and its month-to-month variation. The choice of how to supply data is left open.

particulars.what: The person expects to adjust projections as things happen.
particulars.handling: The plan is re-run whenever dates, guest count, contribution or spending change, and at least monthly.

inputs.name: Wedding date
inputs.description: The date from which all payment dates are counted. Not yet stated.

inputs.name: Payment schedule
inputs.description: 6k due in 21 days; 50% of the remaining cost 30 days before; 50% 14 days before. Described in conversation; the contract is the source.

inputs.name: Guest count
inputs.description: About 200 invited; final count known the day before the 30-day payment.

inputs.name: Cost per guest or estimated total cost
inputs.description: Needed to estimate the total from the guest count. Not yet provided.

inputs.name: Net monthly income
inputs.description: About 10k per month take-home pay, stable.

inputs.name: Monthly spending
inputs.description: About 5k per month on average, stated from memory. Bank statements or a bank connection could be supplied later.

inputs.name: Current wedding savings
inputs.description: 10k already saved. Where it is held is out of scope.

inputs.name: Family and partner contribution
inputs.description: 20k in total, expected about 2 weeks before the wedding, not yet firm.

process.name: Estimate total wedding cost
process.formula: estimated total cost = guest count x cost per guest (plus any fixed costs, if the person has them)
needs: Cost per guest or estimated total cost
process.produces: Estimated (later confirmed) total wedding cost, as a low, expected and high case
process.cadence: when guest count or prices change

process.name: Work out the three payment amounts
process.formula: payment 1 = 6k; remaining = total cost - 6k; payment 2 = payment 3 = remaining x 50%
process.produces: Amount and due date of each of the three payments

process.name: Work out monthly surplus
process.formula: monthly surplus = net monthly income - monthly spending
process.produces: Amount available to save each month before the wedding

process.name: Confirm contribution timing and amount
process.produces: Confirmed (or still estimated) date and amount of the 20k, an input to s5

process.name: Project wedding fund balance at each payment date (running balance, cash flow forecast style)
process.formula: closing balance = opening balance + inflows (monthly saving, contribution) - outflows (payments due), repeated per period; opening balance starts at current savings
process.produces: Balance of the wedding fund at each payment date, showing any shortfall or surplus

process.name: Work out monthly saving needed to cover any shortfall (savings goal style)
process.formula: monthly saving needed = shortfall before a payment date / months until that payment date
process.produces: Required monthly saving per payment, set against the monthly surplus from s3

process.name: Review results and decide updates
process.produces: Plain explanation of whether the plan is on track, which assumptions (guest count, contribution date, spending) matter most, and what to update next
process.cadence: monthly and after the guest count is confirmed

definition_of_done.text: The person can see, for each of the three payments, how much is due, when, and whether the wedding fund covers it on that date.
The plan is refreshed at least monthly, and straight away when the guest count is confirmed or the contribution date or amount changes.
All calculations run as tested code and give the same answer each time; the person can trace each number back to its inputs.
The person feels less stressed about the money because they know in advance of any shortfall.

open_questions.text: What is the wedding date? Without it the payment dates cannot be fixed.
What is the cost per guest, or the expected total cost? The size of the shortfall depends on it.
Does the 6k count toward the total cost, so that 'remaining cost' means total minus 6k?
Is the 5k monthly spending a reliable average, and does it include all regular costs? Bank statements or a bank connection could help; the format is still to be decided.
How firm is the 20k contribution, and will it really arrive about 2 weeks before the wedding?
Does the person have other costs apart from the venue payments (for example attire, travel or rings) that should be added to the plan?

Steps s5 and s6 are written as plain arithmetic (a running balance and a simple division); their names only echo 'cash flow forecast' and 'savings goal'. Should they carry those methods? 'Cash flow forecast' has a saved source; 'savings goal' has none yet, so it stays a proposed definition.
Where to hold the money (cash or savings) and the wider budget are out of scope for now and could be a later piece of work.
